frozen_original.description_long: On September 19, 2025, President Donald Trump signed Proclamation 10973, “Restriction on Entry of Certain Nonimmigrant Workers.” It restricted entry of certain H-1B workers outside the United States unless the petition was accompanied or supplemented by a $100,000 payment, subject to exceptions. It took effect at 12:01 a.m. EDT on September 21, 2025, and assigned employers responsibility for retaining proof of payment before filing covered petitions. The text authorized the Homeland Security secretary to exempt an individual, company, or industry when hiring served the national interest and posed no security or welfare threat. White House guidance said the measure applied to new petitions submitted after the effective time, not previously issued visas or earlier petitions, and did not change renewal fees. The proclamation stated an initial 12-month period absent extension. The documented event is the entry restriction and payment condition; these sources do not establish its overall effect on hiring or visa access.
